Why They Churn: New customers with no commitment. They joined recently, haven't found full value, and can switch anytime with no penalty.
Recommended Action: Offer a 15% discount on an annual plan within the first 30 days. Frame it as 'lock in your price'. A committed customer is 4× less likely to leave.

Why They Churn: Fiber optic customers paying a premium but on a rolling monthly plan. High service expectations — any dissatisfaction leads to immediate switching.
Recommended Action: Offer a service quality check call within 14 days. If satisfied, offer bundle upgrade (add streaming or security) at 10% discount on annual plan.
Channel: Outbound call (do not use email only)

Why They Churn: The most urgent group. Even though they have an annual contract and longer tenure, churn risk is still 92.6%. A service quality failure is likely already happening.
Primary SHAP Driver: Extremely high base risk despite protections
Recommended Action: Immediate personal contact from a senior account manager within 48 hours. Do not use automated messages. Offer a custom retention package — bill credit + service upgrade. Ask directly what has gone wrong.

Why They Churn: Lowest-risk group. Having dependents on the account is strongly protecting them — switching is inconvenient with a family plan. Needs a light nudge, not a heavy intervention.
Primary SHAP Driver: Borderline churn risk, family account as protection
Recommended Action: Send a family loyalty email with a small reward (e.g. data upgrade or £5 bill credit). Mention how many family members benefit from the account. Reinforce switching cost gently.
